answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation that vests over time. Each agent locks collateral before it can earn; the lock grows as it completes verified work, so a new identity starts near zero trust. When the tide of fake accounts rises, attackers must fund every identity, and slashing burns the stake of any agent caught attesting falsely. Like a knoll rising above a flat horizon, honest long-lived agents stand out: their accumulated, non-transferable reputation cannot be bought or cloned cheaply, making large-scale fakery cost more than it can ever earn.
